correctness.rationale: Exact interval decomposition and gap count prove the all-index formula. Reflection ensures a≥q. Disjoint n<n0 regime yields a strictly positive formula for all indices at least 3; after n0 the reversed gap sum is an (effectively finite) sum of convex hinges, so the difference is discretely concave; positivity at the bridge n0≥4 is certified by the explicit lower bound. Handles n0≤3 and n=2 separately. Independent finite checker records 5940 exact, 11520 support and 4940 boundary checks, with full proofs carrying the infinite quantifiers.

value.rationale: The 2020 published Question 4.1 is explicitly about the shape of positive Buchweitz indices. The infinite two-block family is a natural lowest-complexity nontrivial test class. A complete classification for all gap sizes and both block lengths plus a closed all-index formula is structural progress beyond constructing isolated interval examples or applying generic eventual sumset growth. Does not claim arbitrary finite-set classification.
